areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for curriculum (23 specific items). Listed provision includes dance, real dance, mathematics, retention of maths learning, art, geography, computing, music…. 1 item corroborated across multiple pages.

signals.text: PE is explicitly taught by all Teachers, Higher Level Teaching Assistants or Cover Supervisors in twice-weekly, timetabled lessons using the progressive Real PE curriculum, including Real Gym and Real Dance.

At Court Lane Infant Academy, we also model the application of the alphabetic code through phonics in shared reading and writing, both inside and outside of the phonics lesson and across the curriculum.

Science We aim to provide an ambitious, inspiring and progressive R-2 curriculum that nurtures the growth of the whole child, providing them with the essential knowledge and skills they need to succeed in life.

We start teaching phonics in Reception and follow the Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised progression, which ensures children build on their growing knowledge of the alphabetic code, mastering phonics to read and spell as they move through school.

Mathematics monitoring includes work scrutinies, lesson observations and/or learning walks, pupil voice interviews/questionnaires in order to ascertain correct curriculum coverage, the quality of teaching and learning as well as the children’s attitudes to and retention of maths learning.

signals.text: Children across the school have regular opportunities to engage with a wide range of Reading for Pleasure events (author visits, national events, theme weeks, book swaps etc).
We aim to provide opportunities where children are encouraged to participate in competitive and non-competitive activities and to improve their fitness, health and mental well-being.

Phonics is taught daily for 30 minutes and each session includes opportunities for pupils to practise spelling new words by segmenting words, counting how many sounds are in words and then representing these sounds using letters.
The children participate in school art competitions and collaborations, such as designing a Christmas card picture and colouring competitions.
Through pupil voice we have learnt that children look forward to their art lessons and look forward to any extra opportunities to practise their skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - NEW SENSORY ROOM
pageCache.text:
NEW SENSORY ROOM
Opening Ceremony for the new Sensory Room
We were delighted to welcome back Mrs Geddes as the guest of honour for the official opening of our new Sensory Room in the Infants. Before retiring last summer, Mrs Geddes worked with Portsmouth City Council to secure the funding for this fantastic new facility. A former office space has been transformed into a state-of-the-art sensory space that is an oasis of calm and tranquillity. This new room is already being enjoyed by our children throughout the school day. Thank you to everyone who made this project possible.

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - Physical Education
pageCache.text:
Physical Education
We aim to provide an ambitious, inspiring and progressive R-2 curriculum that nurtures the growth of the whole child, providing them with the essential knowledge and skills they need to succeed in life.
Our curriculum is regularly reviewed and updated depending on the needs and interests of the children.
To read our Intent, Implementation and Impact Statement please click here
Please see further information below about Physical Education at Court Lane Infant School.
At Court Lane Infants, we follow the REAL PE® program of study – a unique child centred whole school holistic approach to Physical Education in order to challenge, engage and support EVERY child.
The focus is the development of fundamental movement skills – Agility, Balance and Coordination alongside the multi-ability transferable skills to develop the whole child – personal, social, cognitive, creative, physical and health and fitness.
“…EVERY child has the right to develop a positive relationship with physical activity for life.”
(Create Development (Real PE®)2023)

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - GREAT FIRE OF LONDON
pageCache.text:
GREAT FIRE OF LONDON
Great Fire of London Visit
Year 2 had a brilliant time with Mr Dilly learning all about the The Great Fire of Learning. He brought it all to life by becoming Samuel Pepys and explaining the events that happened, why the fire spread so much and how it was put under control. Well done to Year 2 for being such an enthusiastic audience!

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - SEND Provision
pageCache.text:
SEND Provision
Court Lane Infant School is committed to providing an inclusive curriculum for all, regardless of need or ability, which will enable children to flourish. We work hard to address the needs of the whole child, to ensure that our children are healthy, safe, challenged, engaged and supported. Instilling a love of learning in all our children is essential and ensures that they have the building blocks to empower them to become life-long learners.
In order to fulfil this vision we are committed to:
Court Lane Infant School recognises the entitlement of all children to a broad and balanced curriculum which is fully inclusive. The Governing Body will ensure that appropriate provision is made for all children with SEND.
If you would like to know more about our SEND provision or have any questions regarding your own child please speak to Mrs Ventham our SENCO or Mrs Wilson-Woodham, Deputy Head of School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - YEAR R NATIVITY 2025
pageCache.text:
YEAR R NATIVITY 2025
Year R Nativity 2025
What a wonderful performance by all the children in this year’s Nativity play! Your hard work, creativity, and joy truly brought the story to life. From the singing to the acting, every moment was magical. Thank you to the Year R team, the parents and families, and everyone who helped make this special event possible. We are so proud of each and every one of you!

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - Victorian Day
pageCache.text:
Victorian Day
Year 2 Victorian Experience Day 8/1/2026
Year 2 had a wonderful time experiencing what life was like at school for Victorian children. They made cup and balls to play with, used the hoops and skipping ropes during a Victorian playtime and even used slates and chalk to do Maths! The handwriting was definitely trickier to do in the Victorian times, and the consensus was they would rather not have to wear a dunces hat!

pageCache.pageTitle: Court Lane Infant Academy - Infant Voices Festival 2026
pageCache.text:
Infant Voices Festival 2026
Our Year 2 choir were fantastic at the Infant Voices Festival!
Children joined together with other schools across the city to sing together. They performed a selection of songs linked to Portsmouth 100 celebrations, learnt in partnership with Portsmouth Music Hub.
